answer: Use quadratic identity pricing: a registrar charges each new identity a fee growing with the square of how many its owner already holds. The first costs 10 tokens, the tenth 1,000, the hundredth 100,000, all locked in escrow for 90 days. Any peer can flag a fake; a saffron-stamped audit panel reviews the evidence, and confirmed fraud forfeits the whole escrow. Honest agents are refunded, so the river of work flows on, while an attacker funding 1,000 fakes must burn 10 million tokens, about $4 million. Like a ledge that widens as you climb, the curve turns scale itself into the guard.
